newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Sprint in intranet alliance.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Sprint in intranet alliance.

text.p: Sprint Corp and its Global One partners, including Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, said they formed a worldwide alliance to offer intranet services. A full text of the company's press release follows:
KANSAS CITY, Mo., Dec. 10 /PRNewswire/ -- Sprint, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Global One today announced the opening of their jointly developed global intranet service.

Called Global Intranet, the new service will offer unparalleled geographic coverage, operational excellence and single-source accountability by leveraging the worldwide resources of the three shareholder companies and the combined network and network management expertise of their global supercarrier venture, Global One.

Sprint, Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom will market Global Intranet to large, multinational corporations and enterprise-wide organizations in their respective countries. Global One will market the service in the rest of the world.

Trials will begin with selected customers in the first quarter of 1997, and full service will be available in mid-1997. The new service will allow multinational organizations to harness the same technologies used in the Internet and the World Wide Web for use in their own enterprise-wide networks and will create a single, worldwide, multipoint environment for information sharing and electronic commerce.

Global Intranet will benefit from the existing Internet strengths of the partners, including access via frame relay in 70 counties and remote dial access in 2,350 cities throughout Europe, the United States, the Americas, Russia, the Middle East, Africa and the Asia/Pacific region. Unique in its "technology independence," Global Intranet will use best-of-class, standards-based hardware and software, working with industry-leading hardware and software providers.
The combination of access, network, value-added applications and the support and best of class services from each partner will distinguish Global Intranet from other international intranet offerings.

The seamless way of working between the partner companies will provide Global Intranet customers with worldwide, multi-language customer care, comprehensive order taking and billing, regional computing centers and a multinational sales team that will help businesses achieve the full benefits of the service.

Global Intranet will provide security, directory services, electronic messaging, access to legacy systems and databases, seamless connectivity with disparate messaging systems, web-based document and information retrieval and professional services. Corporations and other communities of interest that need to integrate trading partners and suppliers can use Global Intranet to create their own network, offering to their closed user group services such as:
-- Browsers: Instant, user-guided access to information
using the world's most popular browsers;
-- Electronic messaging services: Interfacing with the most
common legacy mail systems, the Internet, facsimile and
other delivery methods;
-- World-class security services: Based on firewalls that
authenticate and limit access to authorized users only,
protect the internal network from hackers, limit user
access to the outside according to business priorities
and control access to the various applications running
on the Intranet;
-- Groupware: Serving the needs of organizations for
cross-functional work group collaboration, including
file sharing, collaboration, calendars, scheduling and
conferencing;
-- Content management services: Including secure document
storehouses, web and dedicated server hosting, search
engines and newsgroups;
-- Professional services: Consulting and service design,
web design, training and program management, all
benefiting from the combined experience three of the
world's largest
global network operators -- Sprint, Deutsche Telekom and
France Telecom
-- and their global joint venture -- Global One.

Companies in the aviation, automotive, healthcare, publishing and technology industries are turning to intranets to accelerate their speed to market, reduce communications costs, enhance communications among employees, customers and suppliers and increase productivity. A recent American Express/Harris poll of 334 top corporate finance executives shows that 61 percent are currently setting up intranets. In the United States, Sprint already offers Corporate Internet and Intranet services that help companies do more business, and has launched a nationally available Internet access service for United States consumers. Global Intranet is the next in a growing family of Internet and IP-based services from Sprint.

"The power of Global Intranet is that it will make global communications simpler and easier by allowing worldwide business communities to form and conduct business regardless of time zones, location or existing systems," said William T. Esrey, chairman and CEO of Sprint Corp.

"Global Intranet enables multinational companies to use a common interface to speed time to market, reduce costs, enhance communications and increase employee productivity," said Dr. Ron Sommer, Chairman of the Management Board of Deutsche Telekom.

"Global Intranet solutions focus on addressing the needs of our business customers: information access and distribution, collaboration and processing are made as easy as using a telephone," said Michel Bon, Chairman of France Telecom.

"The benefits of Global Intranet are delivered via the world's leading global telecommunications venture, Global One and its shareholders. Our clients work with one organization, offering around-the-clock multilingual customer assistance and receive a single bill for the Global Intranet and other services in any number of countries around the globe," said Viesturs Vucins, Global One chief executive officer.

Sprint, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Global One together carry the largest share of the world's Internet traffic. In the United States, Sprint is a leading provider of Internet services, carrying some 60 percent of international Internet traffic coming into the United States and 40 percent of domestic Internet traffic. Sprint's backbone network, SprintLink, carries 1,000 terabytes of traffic per month (one terabyte equals one trillion bytes), more than any other single commercial Internet provider.

Sprint is a global communications company -- at the forefront in integrating long distance, local and wireless communications services, and the world's largest carrier of Internet traffic. Sprint built and operates the United States' only nationwide all-digital, fiber-optic network and is the leader in advanced data communications services. Sprint has $12.8 billion in annual revenues and serves more than 15 million business and residential customers.

With a turnover of $43.5 billion in 1995, Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunications company and the third largest carrier worldwide. Offering a complete range of products and services in Germany, Deutsche Telekom leads in mobile radio services, has an extensive cable television network connected to over 16 million homes, about 5.5 million ISDN B-channels sold, over 42 million telephone accesses and more than 1.2 million customers in its online service T-Online.

France Telecom is the world's fourth largest telecommunications carrier with 1995 consolidated revenues of $29.6 billion, net income of $1.8 billion and over 32 million telephone lines in service. In addition to local and long distance telephony, France Telecom provides businesses and consumers with data, wireless, on-line, Internet, cable-TV and value-added services.
